---
title: "Solution: Diagnostic Plots and Model Comparison"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(broom)
```

```{r fit-models}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
mod1 <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat),                         data = diamonds)
mod2 <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut + color + clarity, data = diamonds)
```

## Task 1: Four diagnostic plots for mod1

```{r task1, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(mod1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Plot 1 — Residuals vs Fitted:
# The points form bands (striped pattern) due to the discrete nature of
# cut/color/clarity — the model cannot capture these effects with carat alone.
# The red LOESS line deviates from zero, indicating remaining structure.

# Plot 2 — Normal Q-Q:
# Points follow the diagonal reasonably well in the middle, but deviate
# in the tails — the residuals are slightly heavy-tailed. This is acceptable
# for this large dataset; it will not invalidate inference badly.

# Plot 3 — Scale-Location:
# The LOESS line is not flat — variance is not fully constant. The log
# transformation has improved homoscedasticity over the raw scale, but
# further improvement would come from adding quality variables.

# Plot 4 — Residuals vs Leverage:
# No diamond has Cook's distance close to 1. There are some high-leverage
# observations (extreme carat values), but none is catastrophically influential.
```

## Task 2: AIC comparison

```{r task2}
AIC(mod1, mod2)

delta_aic <- AIC(mod1) - AIC(mod2)
cat("ΔAIC:", round(delta_aic, 1), "\n")

# mod2 has a dramatically lower AIC (by > 2,000 units).
# A ΔAIC > 10 is strong evidence; > 100 is overwhelming.
# The quality variables (cut, color, clarity) provide massive improvement.
```

## Task 3: F-test for the extra predictors

```{r task3}
anova(mod1, mod2)

# The F-statistic is extremely large (>> 100) with p-value < 2.2e-16.
# This confirms that the 17 extra parameters (cut, color, clarity dummies)
# are jointly highly significant — they explain enormous amounts of
# residual variance. The F-test and AIC agree: use mod2.
```

## Task 4: Residuals vs fitted for mod2

```{r task4}
aug2 <- augment(mod2)

ggplot(aug2, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x,
              colour = "red", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title    = "Residuals vs Fitted — mod2 (log-log + cut + color + clarity)",
    subtitle = "The LOESS line is much closer to zero than for mod1. Variance more stable.",
    x        = "Fitted log(price)",
    y        = "Residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Compared to mod1, the banded pattern has largely disappeared.
# The LOESS line is nearly flat around zero, and the spread of residuals
# is more uniform across fitted values. Some heteroscedasticity remains
# at the extremes of fitted price, but the model is substantially better.
```
